name: Barbell back squat
setup: Set the bar at mid-chest height. Bar across the upper traps (high bar) or slightly lower on the rear delts (low bar), hands just outside the shoulders. Feet about shoulder-width, toes turned out 15–30°.
steps: Breathe into your belly and brace, then unrack and walk back two or three short steps. | Break at the hips and knees together and sit down between your heels, knees tracking over your toes. | Go down until the hip crease is at or just below the top of the knee, or as deep as you can keep your lower back neutral. | Drive up through the whole foot, chest and hips rising at the same rate. Breathe out near the top and re-brace before the next rep.
cues: Spread the floor with your feet | Bar stays over mid-foot | Chest proud, eyes slightly down | Brace before every rep
mistakes: Knees caving inward on the way up | Hips shooting up first, turning it into a good morning | Heels lifting or weight drifting to the toes | Losing the brace and rounding at the bottom

name: Leg press
setup: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad. Feet hip- to shoulder-width in the middle of the platform. Press the sled up and release the safety handles.
steps: Lower the sled under control by bending your knees toward your chest. | Stop when your knees are around 90°, or just before your lower back starts to peel off the pad. | Press through your mid-foot and heels back to the top. | Finish with the knees almost straight, without snapping them into lockout.
cues: Hips glued to the seat | Knees track in line with your toes | Smooth turnaround, no bounce
mistakes: Going so deep that the pelvis tucks and the lower back rounds | Locking the knees hard at the top | Pushing your hands on your knees to help | Bouncing out of the bottom

name: Bulgarian split squat
variant: Dumbbells, rear foot on a bench
setup: Stand about a long stride in front of a knee-height bench and rest the laces of your rear foot on it. Hold dumbbells at your sides. Your front foot should be far enough forward that the heel stays down at the bottom.
steps: Lower straight down, letting the rear knee travel toward the floor. | Keep the front knee tracking over the toes; a slight forward lean of the torso brings in more glute. | Stop when the rear knee is just above the floor or the front thigh is about parallel. | Drive through the front mid-foot to stand. Finish all reps on one leg, then switch.
cues: Elevator down, not forward | Rear leg is just a kickstand | Front heel stays heavy
mistakes: Stance too short, so the front heel lifts | Pushing off the back foot | Front knee caving inward | Rushing reps and losing balance; hold a rack with one hand if you need to

name: Single-leg explosive Zercher squat
variant: Zercher split squat, controlled down and explosive up
setup: Hold the bar in the crooks of your elbows with your hands clasped and upper arms tight to your ribs. A pad or towel on the bar helps. Take a split stance, rear heel up.
steps: Lower under control until the rear knee is just above the floor. | Keep your chest up and elbows up as the bar tries to pull you forward. | Drive up hard and fast through the front foot. | Finish all reps on one side, then switch.
cues: Elbows up, chest up | Control down, explode up | Front foot does the work
mistakes: Upper back rounding under the bar | Front knee caving inward | Bouncing the rear knee off the floor
note: Shown as a split squat with the rear foot on the floor. Lower slowly, then drive up as fast as you can.

name: Hack squat single-leg step-up
setup: Use a box high enough that your thigh is about parallel with the foot on it. Hold dumbbells at your sides and place the whole working foot on the box.
steps: Lean slightly forward over the front foot. | Drive through the heel of the front leg to stand fully on the box. The back foot should do as little as possible. | Stand tall at the top. | Lower under control on the same leg back to the start.
cues: Front leg does all the work | Knee tracks over the toes | Slow lowering
mistakes: Pushing off the back foot | Front knee caving inward | Box so high that your back rounds to get up
note: Shown as a loaded step-up onto a box. A hack squat machine trains the same muscles in a two-leg squat pattern.

name: Leg extension
setup: Sit back against the pad with your knee joint lined up with the machine's pivot. The roller pad sits on the lower shin just above the ankle. Hold the side handles.
steps: Extend your knees until your legs are nearly straight. | Squeeze your quads for a one-second pause at the top. | Lower under control to about 90° of knee bend.
cues: Sit tall, hips down | Pause and squeeze at the top | Control the lowering
mistakes: Kicking or swinging the weight up | Hips lifting off the seat | Knee not lined up with the pivot, which strains the joint

name: Standing calf raise
setup: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step edge and your heels free. Knees straight but not locked. Hold a support or load.
steps: Lower your heels slowly into a deep stretch. | Pause for 1–2 seconds at the bottom to take the bounce out. | Rise as high as you can onto the big toe. | Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly.
cues: Pause at the bottom | Push through the big toe | Knees stay straight
mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom | Short, fast reps | Bending the knees to cheat the weight up
note: Bent-knee (seated) calf raises shift more of the work to the soleus.

name: Seated calf raise
setup: Sit with the pad snug on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform edge, heels free.
steps: Lower your heels into a deep stretch and pause for 1–2 seconds. | Push up through the balls of your feet as high as you can. | Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly.
cues: Pause in the stretch | Full height at the top | Slow tempo
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom | Short range | Rocking the torso to move the pad
note: With the knees bent the gastrocnemius goes slack, so this trains the soleus underneath it.

name: Tibialis raise
variant: Back against a wall, or a tib bar
setup: Lean your back against a wall with your heels about a foot out in front of you, legs straight.
steps: Keeping your heels on the floor, pull your toes up toward your shins as far as you can. | Hold briefly at the top. | Lower your toes slowly.
cues: Heels stay down | Toes to shins | Control the lowering
mistakes: Bending the knees | Short range | Rushing the reps
note: Useful for runners and for balancing all the calf work. Make it harder by walking your feet further from the wall or using a tib bar.

name: Romanian deadlift
setup: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand grip just outside your thighs, feet hip-width, knees soft. Pull your shoulders back and tighten your lats.
steps: Push your hips straight back while the bar slides down the front of your thighs. | Keep your spine neutral and knees only slightly bent; your shins stay close to vertical. | Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch, usually around mid-shin, without your back rounding. | Drive your hips forward to stand up and squeeze your glutes. Don't lean back at the top.
cues: Hips back, not down | Keep the bar touching your legs | Proud chest, long neck
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach lower | Bending the knees too much so it becomes a squat | Letting the bar drift away from the legs | Leaning back at lockout

name: Conventional deadlift
setup: Stand with feet hip-width and the bar over your mid-foot, about an inch from your shins. Hinge down and grip just outside your legs. Push your hips back until your shins touch the bar: chest up, back flat, shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
steps: Brace hard and pull the slack out of the bar so it's tight before it leaves the floor. | Push the floor away, keeping the bar against your legs and your back angle steady until the bar passes the knees. | Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes. | Lower by pushing the hips back first, then bend the knees once the bar passes them.
cues: Bar over mid-foot | Pull the slack out first | Lats tight, bar close
mistakes: Rounding the back off the floor | Hips shooting up so it turns into a stiff-leg pull | Bar drifting forward away from the shins | Leaning back hard at lockout

name: Trap bar deadlift
variant: Hex bar, high or low handles
setup: Step inside the bar with your feet hip-width and the handles centred on your feet. Push your hips back and down to grab the handles. Chest up, shoulders over or slightly in front of the handles, lats tight.
steps: Brace your midsection. | Push the floor away so your hips and shoulders rise together. | Stand tall and squeeze your glutes, without leaning back. | Return by pushing the hips back first, then bending the knees, keeping your back neutral.
cues: Push the floor away | Hips and shoulders rise together | Squeeze oranges in your armpits
mistakes: Rounding the back off the floor | Jerking the bar instead of taking up the slack | Over-leaning back at lockout | Hips shooting up first

name: Hip thrust
variant: Barbell, upper back on a bench
setup: Rest your upper back, just below the shoulder blades, on the edge of a bench. Roll a padded bar over your hip crease. Feet flat about hip-width, placed so your shins are vertical at the top.
steps: Brace and tuck your chin. | Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is parallel to the floor. | Squeeze your glutes for a second with the pelvis slightly tucked. | Lower under control.
cues: Ribs down, chin tucked | Shins vertical at the top | Push through the heels
mistakes: Arching the lower back to get higher | Feet too far out (hamstrings take over) or too close (quads take over) | Pushing through the toes

name: Prone leg curl
setup: Lie face down with your knees just off the end of the pad, lined up with the machine's pivot. The roller pad sits just above your heels. Hold the handles.
steps: Press your hips into the pad. | Curl your heels toward your glutes as far as the machine allows. | Pause for a moment at the top. | Lower over 2–3 seconds to almost straight legs.
cues: Hips stay down | Pull with the heels, not the lower back | Slow on the way down
mistakes: Hips lifting off the pad to finish the rep | Cutting the range short at either end | Letting the weight drop

name: Nordic hamstring curl
setup: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under something solid or held by a partner. Keep a straight line from knees to head with your hips extended.
steps: Lean forward slowly, resisting with your hamstrings and keeping your hips straight. | Go as far as you can control, then catch yourself with your hands. | Push lightly off the floor and pull yourself back up with your hamstrings.
cues: Hips stay straight | Fight the fall | Slow, 3–5 second lowering
mistakes: Bending at the hips to make it easier | Dropping fast once it gets hard | Doing too much too soon, which leaves you very sore
note: Nordic curls have good evidence for lowering hamstring injury risk, which matters for runners and sprinters. Build up from a few reps.

name: Adductor / abductor machine
setup: Sit with your back against the pad. For adductors the pads sit on the inside of your knees; for abductors, on the outside. Start the range at a comfortable stretch.
steps: Adductor: squeeze your legs together. Abductor: push them apart. | Pause for a second at the end of the range. | Return slowly to the stretch.
cues: Sit tall | Control the stretch | Pause at the end
mistakes: Letting the weight stack slam | Using momentum | Starting too wide before you've built up to it, which can strain the groin
note: On the abductor, leaning forward slightly shifts more of the work to the glutes.

name: Flat bench press
setup: Lie with your eyes under the bar. Pull your shoulder blades back and down, keep a slight arch, glutes on the bench, feet planted. Grip slightly wider than shoulder-width with wrists stacked over the elbows. Unrack to straight arms over your shoulders.
steps: Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows about 45–70° from your torso. | Touch the chest lightly, with no bounce. | Press up and slightly back so the bar finishes over your shoulders. | Keep your shoulder blades pinned and feet driving the whole set.
cues: Bend the bar apart | Leg drive into the floor | Forearms vertical under the bar
mistakes: Elbows flared out to 90° | Bouncing the bar off the chest | Hips lifting off the bench | Wrists bent back

name: Incline bench / dumbbell press
setup: Set the bench to 30–45°. Sit with the dumbbells on your thighs, kick them up as you lie back, and pull your shoulder blades back and down. Start with the weights at the sides of your upper chest, forearms vertical.
steps: Press up and slightly in until the dumbbells nearly touch over your upper chest. | Lower under control to a deep stretch at chest level, elbows about 45–60° from your torso. | Keep your shoulder blades set against the bench throughout.
cues: Forearms vertical | Press toward the ceiling over your collarbones | Slow, deep lowering
mistakes: Bench set too steep, which turns it into a shoulder press | Elbows flared to 90° | Clanging the dumbbells together at the top | Cutting the stretch short

name: Dips
variant: Parallel bars, assisted or seated machine
setup: Grip the parallel bars and lock your arms, shoulders pushed down away from your ears. A slight forward lean puts more load on the chest; staying upright puts more on the triceps.
steps: Lower by bending your elbows, letting them travel back rather than out. | Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or earlier if your shoulders complain. | Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Shoulders down and back | Elbows point behind you | Controlled depth
mistakes: Sinking too deep with the shoulders rolling forward | Shrugging at the bottom | Swinging the legs for momentum | Half reps
note: Assisted machine: same movement with a counterweight. Seated dip machine: same pressing pattern while seated; keep the shoulders down.

name: Push-up (with plus)
variant: Bodyweight; add the “plus” at the top for the serratus
setup: Hands slightly wider than your shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels, glutes and abs tight.
steps: Lower your chest toward the floor with your elbows about 45° from your body. | Stop just above the floor. | Press back up to straight arms. | At the top, push the floor away a little further so your upper back rounds slightly and your shoulder blades spread apart. That's the plus.
cues: Body moves as one plank | Elbows at 45° | Push the floor away at the top
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking up | Elbows flared straight out | Half reps

name: Cable chest fly
variant: Cables at or above shoulder height
setup: Set the pulleys at shoulder height or slightly higher. Take a staggered stance in the middle and fix a slight bend in the elbows.
steps: Start with your arms wide and chest stretched. | Bring your hands together in an arc in front of your lower chest. | Squeeze for a moment. | Return slowly to the stretch.
cues: Hug a big tree | Elbow bend stays fixed | Slow on the way back
mistakes: Bending the elbows so it turns into a press | Going too heavy to control the stretch | Letting the shoulders roll forward at the end

name: Pull-ups
setup: Grip the bar overhand, slightly wider than your shoulders. Hang with straight arms, legs together, ribs pulled down.
steps: Start by pulling your shoulder blades down and back. | Drive your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar. | Lower under control all the way to a full hang. | On the assisted machine or a band, keep exactly the same mechanics.
cues: Elbows to your back pockets | Chest up to the bar | No kipping
mistakes: Half reps that stop short of a full hang | Swinging or kicking | Shrugging the shoulders up to the ears | Reaching the chin up instead of pulling the body up

name: Lat pulldown
setup: Set the thigh pad snug. Grip slightly wider than your shoulders and lean back about 10–20°.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down first. | Drive your elbows down to bring the bar to your upper chest. | Pause briefly. | Return slowly to a full stretch with straight arms.
cues: Elbows down to the ribs | Chest up to meet the bar | Full stretch at the top
mistakes: Leaning far back so it becomes a row | Pulling behind the neck | Using momentum | Cutting the stretch short

name: Seated cable row + single-arm finisher
setup: Sit tall with your feet on the platform and knees soft. Grab the handle with arms straight.
steps: Let your shoulders reach forward slightly for a stretch, keeping your back neutral. | Pull the handle to your lower ribs by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Pause for a second, then return under control. | Finish with single-arm cable rows: one arm at a time, elbow close to the body, a little torso rotation is fine.
cues: Lead with the elbows | Chest up, torso still | Squeeze, then stretch
mistakes: Rocking back to swing the weight | Shrugging the shoulders | Pulling with the wrists and biceps instead of the elbows

name: Bent-over row
setup: Hinge forward to about 45° or lower with a neutral spine and soft knees. Overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, bar hanging under your shoulders.
steps: Pull the bar to your lower ribs or upper belly, driving your elbows back. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top. | Lower to straight arms under control without standing up.
cues: Torso stays still | Elbows back toward the hips | Neutral neck
mistakes: Standing up as you row to swing the weight | Rounding the back | Jerking the bar off the bottom

name: Chest-supported T‑bar row
variant: Machine, chest on an angled pad
setup: Set the chest pad so you can reach the handles with straight arms. Stand on the foot plates and lean your chest into the pad, with its top edge around your upper chest. A neutral grip biases the lats and mid back; a wide overhand grip biases the upper back and rear delts.
steps: Start from a full stretch: arms straight, shoulder blades allowed to spread. | Pull the handles toward your lower chest by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Pause for a second without lifting your chest off the pad. | Lower under control back to the full stretch.
cues: Chest glued to the pad | Lead with the elbows | Full stretch at the bottom
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad to heave the weight up | Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears | Cutting the stretch short at the bottom
note: The pad takes the lower back out of the lift, so your upper back can be pushed harder without the lower back being the limit.

name: Back extension
variant: 45° bench, bodyweight or holding a plate
setup: Set the pad just below your hip crease so you can bend freely at the hips. Hook your heels under the foot pads and cross your arms over your chest, or hold a plate.
steps: Lower your torso by bending at the hips until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. | Raise back up by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings and extending your back. | Stop when your body is in a straight line with your legs. | Pause, then lower under control.
cues: Hinge at the hips | Squeeze the glutes at the top | Stop at a straight line
mistakes: Swinging up fast with momentum | Over-arching past straight at the top | Pad set so high you can't bend at the hips
note: Keeping the back flat puts more of the work on the glutes and hamstrings; letting it round down and back up shifts more to the spinal erectors.

name: Shoulder press
setup: Set the back pad nearly upright. Sit with the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward or slightly turned in, forearms vertical.
steps: Press up until your arms are straight overhead, dumbbells drifting slightly in. | Lower under control to about ear or shoulder height. | With a barbell: start from the front of the shoulders, move your head back as the bar passes, then push it through. On a machine: set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height.
cues: Ribs down, glutes tight | Forearms vertical | Press up, not forward
mistakes: Arching the lower back to finish the rep | Partial reps that stop well above the shoulders | Elbows pulled behind the body | Bouncing out of the bottom

name: Cable lateral raise
setup: Set the pulley low. Stand side-on and hold the handle in the hand farther from the machine, with the cable running in front of your body.
steps: Raise your arm out to the side to about shoulder height, leading with the elbow and keeping a slight bend. | Pause briefly. | Lower slowly all the way down.
cues: Reach out, not up | Lead with the elbow | Shoulder stays down
mistakes: Shrugging the traps | Swinging the torso | Going heavy enough that the form breaks

name: Rear delt fly
variant: Reverse pec deck or bent-over dumbbells (dumbbells shown)
setup: Machine: chest against the pad, handles at shoulder height, arms straight out in front. Dumbbells: hinge until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, weights hanging under your shoulders.
steps: Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc until they're in line with your body. | Pause for a moment. | Return slowly.
cues: Push the hands wide, not back | Soft, fixed elbows | Shoulders stay down
mistakes: Shrugging | Using momentum | Bending the elbows a lot, which turns it into a row

name: Face pull
variant: Cable with a rope, set at head height
setup: Set a rope at about face height. Hold it with your thumbs pointing back toward you, step back until your arms are straight, and stand tall.
steps: Pull the rope toward your face, driving your elbows high and out to the sides. | Finish with your hands beside your ears and knuckles pointing to the ceiling, like a double-biceps pose. | Pause, then return under control to straight arms.
cues: Elbows high | Pull the rope apart | Hands finish behind the elbows
mistakes: Leaning back to use body weight | Elbows dropping so it turns into a row | Shrugging the shoulders up
note: For direct rotator cuff work, cable or band external rotations are a good addition.

name: Prone Y-raise
variant: Chest on an incline bench, light dumbbells or plates
setup: Set a bench at 30–45° and lie face down on it, chest supported, arms hanging straight down and holding light weights with thumbs up.
steps: Raise your arms forward and up into a Y shape, in line with your body. | Keep a slight bend in the elbows and draw the shoulder blades down and back. | Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
cues: Thumbs up | Shoulders down, away from the ears | Light weight, strict reps
mistakes: Shrugging as the arms rise | Going so heavy that the lower back arches | Swinging the weights up

name: Dumbbell shrug
setup: Stand tall holding heavy dumbbells at your sides with your arms straight.
steps: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can. | Hold the top for a second. | Lower slowly to a full stretch with the shoulders relaxed down.
cues: Straight up, straight down | Arms are just hooks | Pause at the top
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles | Bending the elbows to help | Short, bouncy reps

name: Neck flexion & extension
variant: Plate on a bench, band or neck harness
setup: For flexion, lie face up on a bench with your head off the end and a light plate on a folded towel on your forehead. For extension, lie face down and hold the plate on the back of your head, or use a harness.
steps: Let your head lower slowly to a comfortable stretch. | Tuck your chin and curl your head up toward your chest. | Pause, then lower slowly. Train extension the same way, face down.
cues: Start very light | Slow and controlled | Pain-free range only
mistakes: Going heavy too soon | Jerking the head | Pushing into a painful range
note: Neck strength matters for contact and combat sports. Progress slowly: the neck adapts well but gets irritated by sudden jumps in load.

name: Biceps curl / preacher curl
setup: Stand tall with the weights at your sides, palms forward, elbows by your ribs. On the preacher bench, set it so your armpits sit over the top of the pad with your upper arms flat on it.
steps: Curl the weight up without letting the elbows drift forward much. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower over 2–3 seconds to a full stretch. | On the preacher bench the bottom of the rep is the hardest part, so control it rather than letting it drop.
cues: Elbows pinned | Full stretch at the bottom | No hip swing
mistakes: Swinging with the hips or lower back | Stopping short of straight arms | Elbows travelling forward to shorten the lever

name: Hammer curl
setup: Stand with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing each other.
steps: Curl up, keeping the neutral grip and the elbows pinned. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Thumbs up | Elbows still | Slow lowering
mistakes: Swinging the weights up | Elbows drifting forward | Turning the palms up partway through

name: Reverse curl
variant: EZ bar or barbell, overhand grip
setup: Stand tall holding the bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width, elbows by your sides.
steps: Curl the bar up, keeping your wrists straight and knuckles up. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Knuckles up, wrists straight | Elbows pinned | Slow lowering
mistakes: Wrists bending back | Swinging the hips | Going too heavy for the forearms to control

name: Single-arm triceps extension
setup: Sit or stand holding one dumbbell overhead, upper arm vertical beside your head. Your free hand can hold the working elbow in place.
steps: Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending only at the elbow. | Go into a deep stretch while the upper arm stays still. | Extend back to a straight arm.
cues: Elbow points to the ceiling | Ribs down | Only the forearm moves
mistakes: Elbow flaring out to the side | Upper arm swinging forward and back | Arching the lower back

name: Single-arm triceps pushdown
setup: Set the pulley high and stand close with a slight forward lean, elbow tucked at your side.
steps: Push the handle down until your arm is straight. | Pause at the bottom. | Let it come back up to about 90° without the elbow drifting forward.
cues: Elbow glued to the ribs | Only the forearm moves | Full lockout
mistakes: Elbow moving forward and back | Leaning over the handle to push with body weight | Stopping short of lockout

name: Farmer's carry
setup: Pick up heavy dumbbells with a deadlift motion and stand tall, arms straight, shoulders back and down.
steps: Walk with short, controlled steps. | Keep your torso upright without leaning to either side. | Walk for a set distance or time, then put the weights down with a flat back.
cues: Crush the handles | Tall posture, ribs down | Short, quick steps
mistakes: Shoulders rounding forward | Leaning or twisting | Dropping the weights with a rounded back

name: Cable crunch
variant: Kneeling, rope from a high pulley
setup: Kneel facing a high pulley and hold the rope beside your head. Sit your hips back slightly; they stay still for the whole set.
steps: Curl your ribs down toward your pelvis, rounding your spine. | Bring your elbows toward your thighs while the hips stay put. | Squeeze your abs at the bottom. | Uncurl under control back to the start.
cues: Ribs to hips | Round the spine, don't hinge | Hips stay still
mistakes: Sitting back and pulling with the hips | Pulling the rope down with the arms | Fast, jerky reps

name: Hanging leg raise
variant: From a pull-up bar; bent knees make it easier
setup: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, arms straight and shoulders pulled down.
steps: Raise your legs in front of you, keeping them as straight as you can. | At the top, curl your pelvis up so your lower back rounds slightly. That's where the abs work hardest. | Lower slowly without swinging.
cues: Curl the pelvis up | No swinging | Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the legs for momentum | Lifting the legs with no pelvic curl, which is mostly hip flexor work | Dropping the legs fast

name: Cable rotational chop (high to low)
setup: Set the cable high. Stand side-on to the machine, feet wider than your shoulders, and grip the handle with both hands up by the pulley.
steps: Rotate through your hips and torso together, pulling the handle diagonally down across your body toward the opposite hip. | Keep your arms mostly straight; they're just levers. | Let the back foot pivot as you turn. | Return under control and finish all reps before switching sides.
cues: Turn from hips and ribs together | Arms are just levers | Smooth and controlled
mistakes: Pulling with the arms only | Bending or rounding the lower back | Going so heavy you lose speed and control

name: Barbell clean
variant: Power clean from the floor; the hang clean is the easier version
setup: Feet hip-width, bar over the mid-foot, grip just outside the knees. Shoulders slightly in front of the bar, back flat, arms straight.
steps: First pull: push the floor away and keep the bar close, holding your back angle until the bar passes the knees. | Second pull: as the bar reaches the upper thigh, jump. Extend hips, knees and ankles hard and shrug. | Pull yourself under the bar and whip the elbows around fast. | Catch it on the front of your shoulders with elbows high in a quarter squat, then stand up.
cues: Bar close the whole way | Jump and shrug | Fast elbows
mistakes: Bending the arms early, which turns it into a reverse curl | Bar swinging forward away from the body | Catching low-elbowed with the weight on your wrists | Hips rising before the shoulders off the floor
note: This is a technical lift. Learn it from the hang with an empty bar, and a session with a coach is worth it.

name: Band pass-through
variant: Light band or broomstick, wide grip
setup: Hold a light band or a broomstick with a wide grip in front of your hips, arms straight.
steps: Raise your arms up and overhead in a wide arc, keeping the elbows straight. | Continue back behind you as far as your shoulders allow without arching your lower back. | Reverse the arc back to the front. Narrow the grip over time as your shoulders loosen.
cues: Elbows locked | Ribs down | Slow and smooth
mistakes: Grip so narrow that the elbows bend | Arching the lower back to get the band behind you

name: Cable external rotation
variant: Cable or band at elbow height
setup: Set a cable at elbow height and stand side-on with the working arm farther from the machine. Bend the elbow to 90° and tuck it against your side; a rolled towel under the arm helps.
steps: Rotate your forearm out, away from your body, keeping the elbow pinned to your side. | Stop when you feel the back of the shoulder working, before the elbow lifts away. | Return slowly across your body.
cues: Elbow glued to your side | Rotate, don't swing | Light weight, slow reps
mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body | Twisting the torso to move the weight | Going heavy

name: Overhead triceps stretch
setup: Stand tall and raise one arm overhead.
steps: Bend the elbow so your hand drops behind your head toward your upper back. | With the other hand, gently press the elbow back and down. | Hold for 30 seconds, breathing slowly, then switch sides.
cues: Ribs down | Gentle pressure | Breathe into it
mistakes: Arching the lower back | Forcing the elbow hard

name: Pronation & supination
variant: Light dumbbell or hammer held at one end
setup: Sit or stand with your elbow bent to 90° at your side, holding a light dumbbell or a hammer by one end, thumb up.
steps: Slowly rotate your palm to face down, letting the weight tip toward the floor. | Rotate back through thumb-up to palm-up. | Keep the elbow still; only the forearm turns.
cues: Elbow pinned | Slow both ways | Hold further from the weight to make it harder
mistakes: Moving the shoulder to help | Using a weight so heavy that the turn gets jerky

name: Wrist flexor & extensor stretch
setup: Hold one arm straight out in front of you, elbow locked.
steps: Palm facing away, fingers up: gently pull the fingers back toward you with the other hand to stretch the underside of the forearm. | Then point the fingers down, palm toward you, and gently press the back of the hand to stretch the top of the forearm. | Hold each for 20–30 seconds.
cues: Elbow straight | Gentle pull | Breathe
mistakes: Bending the elbow | Yanking into pain

name: Wrist curl
variant: Dumbbell, forearm on your thigh or a bench
setup: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm up and wrist just past the edge, holding a light dumbbell.
steps: Let the dumbbell roll toward your fingertips and lower the wrist. | Curl the wrist up as high as you can, squeezing the forearm. | Lower slowly. For the back of the forearm, flip to palm-down for reverse wrist curls.
cues: Forearm stays flat | Full range | Slow lowering
mistakes: Lifting the forearm off the support | Going so heavy that the range shrinks

name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
setup: Kneel on one knee on a pad with the other foot flat in front, both knees at about 90°.
steps: Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and tuck your pelvis slightly under. | Shift your hips forward until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip of the down leg. | Hold 30–45 seconds, then switch. Raising the arm on the stretched side deepens it.
cues: Squeeze the back glute | Tuck the pelvis | Stay tall
mistakes: Arching the lower back instead of moving the hips | Front knee caving inward

name: Cossack squat
variant: Bodyweight, holding a support at first
setup: Stand with a very wide stance, toes turned out slightly.
steps: Shift your weight to one side and sit down into that hip, keeping the heel flat. | Let the other leg straighten, toes pointing up, as you sink. | Go as low as you can control, then push back through the middle and over to the other side.
cues: Heel stays down | Chest up | Hold something for balance at first
mistakes: Heel lifting on the bent leg | Rounding the back to get lower

name: Terminal knee extension
variant: Band anchored in front at knee height
setup: Loop a band around a post at knee height and step into it so it sits behind your knee. Step back to create tension, with your weight on the banded leg.
steps: Let the band pull your knee slightly forward into a bend. | Straighten the knee fully by squeezing your quad, pushing the back of the knee into the band. | Hold the lockout for 2 seconds, then release slowly.
cues: Squeeze the quad hard at lockout | Heel stays down | Slow reps
mistakes: Leaning the hips back instead of straightening the knee | Too little band tension to feel the quad

name: Spanish squat
variant: Heavy band looped behind the knees
setup: Loop a heavy band around a sturdy post at knee height, step inside so it sits behind both knees, and walk back until it's tight.
steps: Sit back and down, letting the band hold your knees so your shins stay vertical. | Lower until your thighs are near parallel with your torso fairly upright. | Hold for 30–45 seconds, or do slow reps.
cues: Shins vertical | Sit back into the band | Weight through the heels
mistakes: Knees drifting forward | Leaning the torso far forward
note: A common rehab drill for patellar tendon pain: it loads the quads hard while keeping stress off the front of the knee.

name: Knee-to-wall ankle mobilisation
variant: Facing a wall, short split stance
setup: Face a wall in a short split stance with your front toes a few centimetres from the wall and hands on the wall.
steps: Keeping the front heel down, drive the front knee forward to touch the wall. | Move the foot back a little each time you can touch easily; that distance is your ankle mobility score. | Do 10–15 slow reps per side.
cues: Heel glued down | Knee tracks over the middle toes | Slow and controlled
mistakes: Heel lifting | Knee caving inward
note: Compare sides: a difference of more than a couple of centimetres is worth working on.

name: Wall calf stretch
variant: Hands on a wall, back leg straight
setup: Stand facing a wall with your hands on it, one foot forward and the other a long step back.
steps: Keep the back leg straight and its heel pressed to the floor. | Lean your hips toward the wall until you feel the stretch high in the back calf. | Hold 30–45 seconds per side. Bending the back knee slightly shifts the stretch lower, into the soleus.
cues: Back heel down | Back toes point forward | Lean, don't bounce
mistakes: Back heel lifting | Back foot turned out

name: Thoracic extension on a foam roller
variant: Foam roller across the upper back
setup: Lie on your back with a foam roller across your upper back, just below the shoulder blades, knees bent and hands supporting your head.
steps: Keep your hips on the floor and your ribs down. | Let your upper back extend over the roller, head and elbows dropping toward the floor behind you. | Pause for a breath, curl back up, then move the roller a few centimetres higher and repeat.
cues: Hips stay down | Move from the upper back, not the lower back | Breathe out as you extend
mistakes: Lifting the hips and arching the lower back | Rolling up onto the neck

name: Thread the needle
setup: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Reach one arm under your body toward the opposite side, letting your upper back rotate and that shoulder drop. | Then sweep the same arm up toward the ceiling, following your hand with your eyes. | Do 8–10 slow reps per side, keeping the hips still.
cues: Hips stay square | Rotate from the upper back | Eyes follow the hand
mistakes: Shifting the hips side to side | Rushing through the range

name: Band pull-apart
setup: Hold a light band at shoulder height with straight arms, hands about shoulder-width apart.
steps: Pull the band apart by moving your hands out to the sides, squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Finish with the band at your chest and your arms in a T. | Return slowly with control.
cues: Arms stay straight | Shoulders down, not shrugged | Squeeze the blades together
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a row | Arching the lower back | Letting the band snap back

name: Wall slide
setup: Stand with your back, head and forearms against a wall, arms in a W with elbows bent to 90°.
steps: Slide your arms up the wall into a Y, keeping forearms and wrists in contact as much as you can. | Feel your shoulder blades rotate up and wrap around your ribs. | Slide back down to the W, pulling the elbows toward your back pockets.
cues: Ribs down, lower back flat | Forearms on the wall | Shoulders away from your ears
mistakes: Arching the lower back to keep the arms on the wall | Shrugging as the arms rise

name: Cat-cow
setup: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
steps: Breathe in and let your belly drop, chest forward, tailbone and head lifting (cow). | Breathe out and round your whole back toward the ceiling, tucking chin and tailbone (cat). | Move slowly through the full range for 8–10 breaths.
cues: Move with your breath | Spread the movement along the whole spine | Arms stay straight
mistakes: Moving only the neck | Rushing

name: Bird dog
setup: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips, spine neutral.
steps: Brace your abs, then reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso. | Hold for 2–3 seconds without letting the hips rotate or the back sag. | Return slowly and switch sides.
cues: Hips level | Reach long, not high | Brace first
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher | Hips rotating open | Moving fast
